paper_metadata.title: Quantum Optimization for Portfolio Management in Financial Services Using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) Algorithm

summary: The paper evaluates VQE for portfolio optimization on a 20‑asset dataset and reports slightly improved financial metrics compared to classical methods: variance 0.0147 vs 0.0152 (MVO) and 0.0155 (BLM), expected return 9.32% vs 8.85%/8.9%, and Sharpe ratio 0.624 vs 0.593/0.608. However, VQE requires 120 s to converge compared to 15 s (MVO) and 25 s (BLM), indicating classical algorithms remain computationally superior in the reported experiment.

experiments.description: VQE-based portfolio optimization on a 20-asset sample portfolio, compared against classical mean-variance optimization and Black-Litterman model; evaluated on simulated and IBM Quantum hardware in a hybrid quantum-classical workflow.

algorithm.variant: standard hybrid VQE for portfolio optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio weights are encoded into a quantum Hamiltonian objective; the paper does not specify a binary/QUBO mapping or qubit-to-variable mapping.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize portfolio risk (variance) while maximizing expected return, formulated as H(w) = alpha * w^T Sigma w - beta * w^T r.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Not specified; described as portfolio optimization with classical constraints and hybrid VQE search.
